about.title: Corning Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Corning sits along Interstate 5 in Tehama County, and many local jobs involve agriculture, trucking, warehousing, or roadside work near busy corridors like I-5 Northbound and Marguerite Avenue. When a workplace injury happens here, California's workers' compensation system is usually the first path for medical care and wage replacement, regardless of who was at fault. But workers' comp isn't always the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate claim against that third party. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't guarantee any result. We simply help injured workers in Corning get in touch with an independent attorney who can look at the details of what happened and explain what options might apply, including any third-party claim tied to a vehicle collision or equipment failure.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Full Picture
items.desc: Because workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer in California, a negligent third party — like a contractor or another driver — may still be separately liable for your injury.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, so getting guidance early can help protect your ability to pursue benefits or a claim.

items.title: Your Job Is Protected From Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand your rights if that happens.

items.question: I was hurt on I-5 while working near Corning — is that a workers' comp case or something else?
items.answer: It could involve both. Workers' compensation typically covers on-the-job injuries regardless of fault, but if another driver caused the crash on I-5, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver. An independent attorney can look at the specifics and explain how the two might work together.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Corning?
items.answer: California generally requires you to notify your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury. Missing that window can complicate your workers' compensation claim, so it's worth acting promptly and documenting what happened.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand what protections apply to your situation.

items.question: What if a subcontractor or equipment company caused my injury, not my employer?
items.answer: If a third party like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, you may be able to file a separate claim against them in addition to any workers' compensation benefits. These third-party claims generally carry a two-year deadline in California, so timing matters.
